pl.text: Plural. Most nouns take -и (чиния → чинии); many one-syllable masculine nouns take -ове (град → градове); neuter -о becomes -а (село → села) and -е becomes -ета (кафе → кафета).

count.text: Count form: after a number or няколко / колко, a masculine noun for a thing takes -а / -я instead of the plural: два стола, пет града. Not for people: двама мъже.

the-full.text: The full article -ът / -ят on a masculine word marks the subject of the sentence (also after съм): Хлябът е на масата.

the-short.text: The short article -а / -я on a masculine word: used whenever it is not the subject, after a preposition or as the object: в града, видях хляба.

the.text: "The" is an ending in Bulgarian: -та for feminine words and masculine words in -а (жената, бащата), -то for neuter (детето), -те or -та in the plural (книгите, децата).

np-bare.text: The noun has no article although it means "the …": the article goes on the first word of the phrase only, here the word before it (новата къща, моят брат).

voc.text: Vocative: the form for addressing someone directly: госпожа → госпожо, Иван → Иване, мама → мамо.

vowel.text: я becomes е when the next syllable has е or и, or when the stress moves: бял → бели, хляб → хлебове, свят → света.

irr.text: An irregular form: it does not follow the usual pattern and is learned as a word of its own (дете → деца, човек → хора, дойда → дошъл).

agr-f.text: Agreement: adjectives, possessives and -л forms take the gender of their noun. -а (or -я) for a feminine noun: нова къща, моя сестра, тя е купила.

agr-n.text: Agreement: -о (or -е) for a neuter noun: ново село, мое дете, то е паднало.

agr-pl.text: Agreement: -и for a plural; in the plural there is one form for all genders: нови къщи, мои приятели, те са дошли.

comp.text: по- before an adjective or adverb means "more": по-голям (bigger), по-бързо (faster). Than = от: по-висок от мен.

sup.text: най- before an adjective or adverb means "most": най-голям (biggest), най-добре (best).

1sg.text: Ending for аз (I): -м (имам, гледам) or -а / -я (чета, говоря) in the present, -х in the past (купих, бях). The verb already says "I", so аз is left out unless stressed.

2sg.text: Ending for ти (you, one person you know well): -ш in the present (имаш, четеш); in the past the form is the same as for той (ти купи).

3sg.text: Ending for той / тя / то (he, she, it): the bare stem in the present (има, чете, говори).

2pl.text: Ending for вие (you, several people or one person politely): -те (имате, четете, купихте).

3pl.text: Ending for те (they): -т in the present (имат, четат, говорят), -ха in the past (купиха).

pres.text: Present tense: what happens now, regularly, or in general.

aor.text: Aorist, the main past tense: an event that happened and finished, the steps of a story: Вчера купих хляб.

impf.text: Imperfect: a past action that was going on or kept happening, the background of a story: Когато четях, телефонът звънна.

perf.text: Perfect: съм + the -л form, for a past event whose result counts now or that you did not see yourself: Ял ли си? (Have you eaten?)

sum-past.text: бях, беше (бе), бяхме, бяхте, бяха: the past of съм (was, were). съм has one past form, for a moment as well as for a longer state.

part-l.text: The -л form of the verb (купил, купила, купило, купили), used after съм (perfect) and бих (conditional); its ending matches the subject.

part-pass.text: A participle in -н / -т: the state after something was done to it (затворен = closed, написано = written); it matches its noun like an adjective.

fut.text: ще + verb makes the future; the verb keeps its normal present ending for the person: ще купя (I will buy), ще дойдеш (you will come).

neg-fut.text: няма да + verb is the negative future: няма да дойда (I will not come). няма does not change for the person; the verb does.

da.text: Bulgarian has no infinitive: "want to go" is искам да отида, and the verb after да takes the person ending as well. At the start of a question да means "shall …": Да отидем ли? (Shall we go?)

cond.text: бих + the -л form means "would": бих искал (I would like). бих changes for the person (би, бихме, бихте, биха).

imp.text: Imperative, a request or command: -и / -й to one person (чети, гледай), -ете / -йте to several or politely (четете, гледайте).

pf.text: Perfective verb (купя, кажа, дойда): one action seen as a whole and completed. It is the form after да and ще for a single action, and in the aorist for a finished event.

ipf.text: Imperfective verb (купувам, казвам, идвам): an action in progress, repeated, or in general. Only an imperfective verb can stand on its own in the present.

se.text: се makes the action turn back on the subject or stand without an object: мия се (I wash myself), казвам се (I am called), вратата се отвори (the door opened).

si.text: си: for or to oneself (купих си кола, I bought myself a car), one's own (Почисти си стаята, clean your room), or a fixed part of the verb (спомням си, I remember). Not the си of "you are" (ти си).

poss-own.text: си after a noun means "one's own" and points back to the subject: Той обича жена си (his own wife).

cl-acc.text: Short object pronoun (ме, те, го, я, ни, ви, ги): it never starts the sentence and stands right next to the verb: Видях го.

cl-dat.text: Short "to" pronoun (ми, ти, му, ѝ, ни, ви, им): "to me", "to him"; it stands right next to the verb: Дай ми хляба.

poss-short.text: After a noun (or next to the verb before it), the short pronoun means "my, your, his …": майка ми (my mother), колата ни (our car), Къде са ми ключовете? The noun usually takes the article (колата ни), but most single family members do not (майка ми, брат ми); син and внук do (синът ми).

poss.text: A long possessive (мой, твой, негов, неин, наш, ваш, техен) takes the gender and number of the thing owned, like an adjective: моя сестра, мои приятели.

long-obj.text: Long object pronoun (мен, теб, него, нея, нас, вас, тях): after a preposition (за мен, с него) or for emphasis.

double.text: Clitic doubling: a short pronoun repeats an object that is already named, often when the object comes first: Ивана я познавам (Ivana, I know her).

li.text: ли turns the sentence into a yes/no question; it stands right after the word the question is about: Идваш ли? (Are you coming?)

ima.text: има means "there is / there are", няма "there isn't / aren't". In this meaning it never changes for the person or for a plural (Има чинии); only the tense changes: имаше (there was), ще има (there will be).

num-pers.text: двама, трима, четирима …: the form of a number for a group of men or a mixed group: двама приятели.

order.text: Short words (ме, ми, се, го, ли, съм, е) cannot start a sentence and stand right after the first stressed word or before the verb, in a fixed order.
